acceptance: RED first: TestLanding_AStopBetweenTheIntentAndTheEmitStillEmitsShipLandedOnce fails before the change.
After the recovery the channel holds exactly one ship.landed with the original event id.
A recovery of a landing whose event is marked sent emits nothing.
Changed functions at 100% coverage on every CI OS; event-channels.md §14 and the package note are updated.
fix: Record in the complete intent that ship.landed is due, with its event id. Mark it sent after the emit. On recovery, emit each due event with no sent mark, with the original event id, so that a consumer drops a duplicate by its idempotency key.
summary: docs/architecture/event-channels.md §14 says ship.landed is at most once: a stop between the write of the complete intent and the emit loses the event. The Agensh router puts unfinished events back into its queue after a restart. Research §2.4 P2.7, §3 F3.7.
title: ship.landed is at least once: the complete intent records the due event, and recovery emits it when it is unsent.
